request:
I help run a trotro station in Accra and I want to keep our routes and fares in one place. Each route goes between two stops, for example Circle to Madina, and has a fare in cedis. I want to add routes and see all of them. Passengers should be able to find out how much it costs to go from one stop to another. Fares go up from time to time, so I need to be able to change the fare of a route.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Is a route the same both ways, so Circle to Madina and Madina to Circle cost the same fare? Or should each direction be added as its own route?
A: Yes. Circle to Madina costs the same as Madina to Circle, so we keep one route for both directions and passengers can ask either way.
Q: If a passenger asks about two stops with no direct route between them, should the system just say there is no route? Or should it work out a trip that changes trotros and add up the fares?
A: Say it was not found. Do not try to join two routes together; only direct routes count.
Q: Should only you and your staff be able to add routes and change fares, while passengers can only look up prices?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built your routes and fares system in `app.py`, with tests in `tests/test_app.py`. All 26 tests pass. Your data is saved in a file called `trotro.db` in the same folder.

**What it does:**
- **POST /routes** adds a route. Send the two stops and the fare, for example `{"stop_a": "Circle", "stop_b": "Madina", "fare": 7.5}`. Each route gets a number automatically.
- **GET /routes** lists every route with its number, its two stops and its fare.
- **GET /fare?from=Circle&to=Madina** gives the fare between two stops. It works either way round: Madina to Circle gives the same fare. If there's no direct route, it says "not found" and never joins two routes together.
- **PATCH /routes/{route number}** changes a route's fare, for example `{"fare": 9}`. If no route has that number, it says "not found".

**What it refuses:**
- A new route with a stop or the fare missing.
- A route where both stops are the same place.
- A fare that isn't a number above zero with at most two decimal places (pesewas). This applies to new routes and fare changes.
- A second route between two stops that already have one, in either order.
- A fare lookup that leaves out one of the stops.

**Choices I made:**
- **Stop names:** spaces at the start or end are ignored, and capital letters don't matter. "madina" and "Madina" count as the same stop, both when checking for repeat routes and when passengers look up a fare.
- **Fares must be written as numbers:** a fare sent as text, such as `"5"`, is refused, even though it looks like a number.
- **Who can make changes:** you had no preference, so anyone using the system can add routes and change fares. There's no login. If you want only you and your staff to be able to make changes, tell me and I can add that.

plan.summary: This plan keeps your trotro routes and fares in one place. Each route joins two stops, such as Circle and Madina, and has one fare in cedis that is the same in both directions. You can add routes, see all of them, and change a route's fare when prices go up. Passengers can give any two stops, in either order, and get the fare if a direct route exists. If there is no direct route, they are told it was not found; routes are never joined together. You had no preference on who may add routes or change fares, so we chose the simplest option: anyone using the system can do everything. Question for you: should adding routes and changing fares be limited to you and your staff, so passengers can only look up prices? This plan does not include that unless you ask for it.

data.name: Route
fields: Route number (given automatically so each route can be picked out)
Fare in cedis (the same in both directions)

endpoints.does: Adds a new route. You give the two stops and the fare in cedis.
Shows every route with its two stops and its fare.
For passengers: give two stops in either order and get the fare of the direct route between them, or a message saying it was not found.
Changes the fare of one route to a new amount.

rules: A new route must have both stops and a fare; refuse it if any of these is missing.
Refuse a route whose two stops are the same place.
The fare must be a number in cedis above zero, with at most two decimal places (pesewas); refuse anything else.
Refuse to add a route between two stops that already have a route, in either order (Circle to Madina and Madina to Circle count as the same route).
A fare lookup works in either order: Circle to Madina and Madina to Circle give the same answer.
If there is no direct route between the two stops asked about, say it was not found. Never join two routes together or add fares up.
A fare lookup must include both stops; refuse it if either is missing.
Changing a fare must be for a route that exists; if it does not, say it was not found.
A new fare must also be a number in cedis above zero, with at most two decimal places; refuse anything else.
